questions.explanation_es: Las plantillas permiten definir la configuración una sola vez y aplicarla de forma consistente en muchos dispositivos, reduciendo errores de configuración manual y el tiempo necesario para aprovisionar o actualizar un gran número de sitios, en comparación con entrar al CLI de cada router uno por uno.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What is a legitimate concern regarding the SD-WAN controllers (vManage, vSmart, vBond) representing a form of centralized dependency in the architecture?

options.A: There is no such concern; centralizing control has literally zero downside in any SD-WAN design
options.B: Because vSmart distributes routing/policy and vManage handles configuration and monitoring, sustained unavailability of these controllers can impair the ability to make new configuration changes or have new routing/policy changes take effect, even though already-established WAN Edge data-plane tunnels generally continue forwarding traffic independently for some time
options.C: If any controller goes down for even one second, every single WAN Edge router immediately loses all connectivity to every other WAN Edge instantly and permanently
options.D: Controller unavailability has no effect on the network at all, since WAN Edge routers do not depend on controllers in any way whatsoever

questions.explanation_es: Dado que vSmart distribuye enrutamiento/política y vManage maneja configuración y monitoreo, la falta de disponibilidad sostenida de estos controladores puede afectar la capacidad de hacer nuevos cambios de configuración o que nuevos cambios de política surtan efecto, aunque los túneles de datos ya establecidos entre WAN Edges generalmente sigan reenviando tráfico de forma independiente por un tiempo — de ahí la importancia de desplegar controladores redundantes.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How can SD-WAN's transport-independent design help an organization during a migration away from an expensive legacy MPLS circuit?

options.A: SD-WAN requires MPLS to be present at every site and cannot function if MPLS is removed
options.B: Because SD-WAN can run its overlay across any mix of transports, an organization can gradually introduce broadband/LTE alongside or instead of MPLS at each site, migrating transport-by-transport or site-by-site without having to redesign the entire overlay policy each time
options.C: SD-WAN transport independence means the organization no longer needs any physical WAN circuit of any kind at all
options.D: Transport independence only applies to data centers and has no relevance to branch site migrations

questions.explanation_es: Como SD-WAN puede correr su overlay sobre cualquier combinación de transportes, una organización puede introducir gradualmente banda ancha/LTE junto con o en reemplazo del MPLS en cada sitio, migrando transporte por transporte o sitio por sitio sin tener que rediseñar toda la política del overlay cada vez — una ventaja concreta de la independencia de transporte.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What operational skill-set shift does adopting SD-WAN typically require from a networking team accustomed to purely traditional box-by-box router configuration?

options.A: No shift is required at all; SD-WAN configuration is byte-for-byte identical to traditional router CLI configuration with no new concepts involved
options.B: Teams typically need to build familiarity with controller-based/centralized policy concepts, templates, and the overlay's control-plane abstractions (like OMP, TLOCs, and centralized policy), in addition to (not instead of) traditional networking fundamentals
options.C: SD-WAN eliminates the need for networking staff to understand IP addressing or routing concepts of any kind ever again
options.D: SD-WAN requires the entire team to become expert C++ software developers before any configuration can be performed

questions.explanation_es: Los equipos suelen necesitar familiarizarse con conceptos de política centralizada/basada en controlador, plantillas, y las abstracciones del plano de control del overlay (OMP, TLOCs, política centralizada), además de (no en reemplazo de) los fundamentos tradicionales de networking — es un salto de habilidades real a considerar en la adopción.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why might Direct Internet Access (DIA) combined with local security inspection at the branch (SD-WAN 'secure branch' design) be preferred over backhauling all internet-bound traffic to a central data center for inspection?

options.A: Backhauling internet traffic to a central site always provides lower latency than accessing the internet locally at the branch
options.B: DIA with local security inspection avoids adding the extra latency and WAN bandwidth cost of backhauling every SaaS/internet request through a central hub, which can meaningfully improve the user experience for cloud applications, provided adequate security controls are deployed at each branch
options.C: DIA eliminates the need for any firewall or security inspection anywhere in the network
options.D: Backhauling is always technically impossible to configure in an SD-WAN environment

questions.explanation_es: El acceso directo a internet (DIA) con inspección de seguridad local evita agregar la latencia extra y el costo de ancho de banda WAN de retroceder cada solicitud SaaS/internet hacia un hub central, lo cual puede mejorar notablemente la experiencia de usuario para aplicaciones en la nube, siempre que se desplieguen controles de seguridad adecuados en cada sucursal.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What is a potential risk of enabling Direct Internet Access (DIA) at many branch sites without adequate local security controls?

options.A: DIA with weak local security expands the organization's attack surface, since each branch now has its own path to the internet that must be independently secured (e.g., firewall, DNS security, malware inspection), rather than relying on a single, more heavily fortified central internet edge
options.B: There is no risk whatsoever; DIA is always strictly safer than centralized internet access under every circumstance
options.C: DIA automatically disables all encryption for every application at the branch
options.D: DIA can only be enabled if the branch site has zero users connected to it

questions.explanation_es: Habilitar DIA sin controles de seguridad locales adecuados amplía la superficie de ataque de la organización, ya que cada sucursal pasa a tener su propio camino a internet que debe asegurarse de forma independiente (firewall, seguridad DNS, inspección de malware), en vez de depender de un único borde de internet central más fortificado.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: How does SD-WAN's ability to define policy centrally help with consistent security segmentation across many branch offices?

options.A: Centralized policy has no relationship to security segmentation whatsoever and only affects routing metrics
options.B: A segmentation policy (e.g., isolating guest traffic from corporate traffic via VPN/VRF segmentation) can be defined once centrally and pushed consistently to every site, rather than requiring an administrator to manually replicate the same segmentation configuration correctly on each individual branch router
options.C: Centralized policy requires every branch to have physically separate cabling for each segment, which SD-WAN cannot avoid
options.D: Segmentation can only be applied to a single branch at a time and cannot be defined centrally under any circumstances

questions.explanation_es: Una política de segmentación (por ejemplo, aislar tráfico de invitados del tráfico corporativo vía segmentación VPN/VRF) puede definirse una sola vez de forma centralizada y aplicarse de forma consistente a cada sitio, en lugar de requerir que un administrador replique manualmente esa misma configuración de segmentación correctamente en cada router de sucursal.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What total cost of ownership (TCO) benefit does SD-WAN's ability to combine cheaper broadband transport with intelligent path selection commonly offer, compared to relying purely on MPLS?

options.A: SD-WAN guarantees that broadband internet will always be technically superior to MPLS in every performance metric with no trade-offs
options.B: By blending lower-cost broadband/LTE transport with MPLS (or replacing MPLS at some sites) while using application-aware routing to protect critical traffic, organizations can often reduce overall WAN transport spend while maintaining acceptable performance for important applications
options.C: TCO benefits only apply if an organization completely eliminates all WAN circuits and relies solely on satellite internet
options.D: SD-WAN always costs more in total than an equivalent pure-MPLS design, with no scenario where it reduces spend

questions.explanation_es: Combinando transporte de menor costo (banda ancha/LTE) con MPLS (o reemplazándolo en algunos sitios) y usando enrutamiento consciente de aplicación para proteger el tráfico crítico, las organizaciones suelen poder reducir el gasto total en transporte WAN manteniendo un rendimiento aceptable para las aplicaciones importantes — un argumento de TCO frecuente a favor de SD-WAN.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: Why is it important to plan bandwidth and licensing sizing carefully on SD-WAN controllers (especially vManage/vSmart) as the number of managed WAN Edge sites grows significantly?

options.A: Controller sizing has no relationship to the number of managed sites; a single minimal controller instance can support any number of sites with zero performance impact
options.B: As the number of WAN Edge devices, control connections, and routes grows, the controllers require adequate compute/scale sizing to handle the increased control-plane load (OMP route processing, template pushes, telemetry ingestion), or performance and responsiveness can degrade
options.C: Controller sizing is only relevant for the physical color of the rack the controllers are mounted in
options.D: Licensing for SD-WAN controllers has nothing to do with the number of WAN Edge devices under management

questions.explanation_es: A medida que crece el número de dispositivos WAN Edge, conexiones de control y rutas, los controladores necesitan un dimensionamiento de cómputo/escala adecuado para manejar la mayor carga del plano de control (procesamiento de rutas OMP, envío de plantillas, ingestión de telemetría), o el rendimiento y la capacidad de respuesta pueden degradarse — una consideración real de diseño al escalar.

questions.name: SD-WAN beneficios/limitaciones
questions.question: What benefit does zero-touch provisioning (ZTP) offer when deploying SD-WAN to many new branch sites?

options.A: ZTP requires an experienced network engineer to be physically on-site at every branch to manually type the full configuration before the device can join the overlay
options.B: ZTP allows a WAN Edge device to be shipped to a branch, connected to power and a transport link by non-technical local staff, and then automatically contact vBond/vManage to receive its identity, software, and configuration with minimal or no manual CLI configuration required on-site
options.C: ZTP eliminates the need for the device to ever have any IP addressing configured, even automatically
options.D: ZTP only functions for wireless access points and has no application to WAN Edge routers

questions.explanation_es: El aprovisionamiento sin intervención (ZTP) permite que un dispositivo WAN Edge se envíe a una sucursal, lo conecte a energía y a un enlace de transporte personal no técnico local, y luego contacte automáticamente a vBond/vManage para recibir su identidad, software y configuración con mínima o ninguna configuración manual de CLI en el sitio — un beneficio operativo clave para desplegar muchas sucursales rápidamente.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In Cisco SD-Access, what happens when a wired endpoint first connects to a Fabric Edge Node and sends its first packet?

options.A: The Fabric Edge Node authenticates/onboards the endpoint (e.g., via 802.1X or MAB), then registers the endpoint's identity (EID) and location with the Fabric Control Plane node, so other nodes can learn how to reach it
options.B: The endpoint's traffic is immediately flooded unencapsulated to every other switch in the entire campus with no registration step of any kind
options.C: The Fabric Border Node handles all endpoint registration directly, and the Fabric Edge Node has no role in this process
options.D: The endpoint must first manually register itself with the Fabric Control Plane using a dedicated software client installed on the endpoint

questions.explanation_es: El Fabric Edge Node autentica/incorpora al endpoint (por ejemplo, vía 802.1X o MAB) y luego registra la identidad (EID) y ubicación de ese endpoint ante el Fabric Control Plane node, para que otros nodos de la fabric puedan aprender cómo alcanzarlo — este registro es análogo a cómo un ITR de LISP registra mapeos EID-a-RLOC.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What role does the LISP protocol play specifically in the SD-Access control plane?

options.A: LISP is used only for encrypting data-plane traffic between Fabric Edge Nodes, with no role in the control plane at all
options.B: LISP provides the mapping mechanism (EID-to-RLOC) that the Fabric Control Plane node uses to track and resolve where endpoints are currently located within the fabric, similar to how LISP is used in a standalone LISP deployment for identity/location separation
options.C: LISP is used exclusively to assign VLAN IDs to fabric-enabled switch ports
options.D: LISP has been fully replaced by BGP EVPN in every SD-Access deployment and is never actually used

questions.explanation_es: LISP provee el mecanismo de mapeo (EID-a-RLOC) que el Fabric Control Plane node usa para rastrear y resolver dónde está actualmente ubicado un endpoint dentro de la fabric, de forma similar a cómo se usa LISP en un despliegue LISP independiente para separar identidad de ubicación.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: How does SGT (Scalable/Security Group Tag) information get carried across the SD-Access fabric data plane?

options.A: SGT information is carried inside the VXLAN header alongside the encapsulated frame, allowing the Fabric Edge Node at the destination to apply SGACL policy based on the source SGT without needing a separate lookup or out-of-band signaling
options.B: SGT information is never transmitted across the network at all; it exists only as a label in the ISE database and has no bearing on actual forwarded packets
options.C: SGT information is carried exclusively via a separate SNMP trap sent to each Fabric Edge Node for every single packet
options.D: SGT information can only be applied if MACsec encryption is also enabled on every link in the fabric

questions.explanation_es: La información de SGT viaja dentro del encabezado VXLAN junto con el frame encapsulado, permitiendo que el Fabric Edge Node en el destino aplique política SGACL basándose en el SGT de origen sin necesitar una consulta separada ni señalización fuera de banda — esto es lo que hace posible la microsegmentación consistente en toda la fabric.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What is the function of the 'Map-Server/Map-Resolver' role within the SD-Access Fabric Control Plane node?

options.A: The Map-Server/Map-Resolver role stores and answers queries about EID-to-RLOC mappings, similar in concept to how a DNS server resolves names to IP addresses, allowing other fabric nodes to discover the current location of any registered endpoint
options.B: The Map-Server/Map-Resolver role is solely responsible for issuing DHCP leases to every endpoint in the fabric
options.C: The Map-Server/Map-Resolver role only functions for wireless endpoints and has no relevance to wired endpoints in the fabric
options.D: The Map-Server/Map-Resolver role encrypts all traffic between the Fabric Border Node and external networks

questions.explanation_es: El rol de Map-Server/Map-Resolver almacena y responde consultas sobre mapeos EID-a-RLOC, de forma conceptualmente similar a cómo un servidor DNS resuelve nombres a direcciones IP, permitiendo que otros nodos de la fabric descubran la ubicación actual de cualquier endpoint registrado.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: In SD-Access, what is a 'virtual network' (VN), and how does it relate to a VRF?

options.A: A virtual network in SD-Access is a macro-segmentation construct that maps to an underlying VRF instance, providing a fully isolated Layer 3 routing domain (for example, separating a 'Guest' virtual network from an 'Employee' virtual network) on top of which SGT-based micro-segmentation can further be applied within each VN
options.B: A virtual network is simply another name for a VLAN, with no relationship to VRF or Layer 3 isolation at all
options.C: A virtual network is used exclusively to identify a specific wireless SSID, with no relevance to wired fabric segmentation
options.D: A virtual network and a VRF are mutually exclusive concepts that cannot be used together in the same fabric

questions.explanation_es: Una virtual network (VN) en SD-Access es un constructo de macro-segmentación que se mapea a una instancia VRF subyacente, proveyendo un dominio de enrutamiento de Capa 3 completamente aislado (por ejemplo, separando una VN 'Invitados' de una VN 'Empleados'), sobre el cual además se puede aplicar micro-segmentación basada en SGT dentro de cada VN.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: How does the SD-Access data plane (VXLAN) support carrying Layer 2 traffic across what is fundamentally a routed (Layer 3) underlay?

options.A: VXLAN cannot carry Layer 2 traffic under any circumstances; SD-Access data plane traffic is always purely Layer 3
options.B: VXLAN encapsulates the original Ethernet frame (including its Layer 2 header) inside a UDP/IP packet, allowing that Layer 2 frame to be transported across the routed underlay between Fabric Edge Nodes, effectively creating an overlay Layer 2 segment (per VNI) on top of Layer 3 transport
options.C: VXLAN requires the underlay itself to be a pure Layer 2 network with no routing at all, contradicting SD-Access's routed-access design
options.D: VXLAN only supports carrying IP multicast traffic and cannot transport regular unicast Ethernet frames

questions.explanation_es: VXLAN encapsula el frame Ethernet original (incluyendo su encabezado de Capa 2) dentro de un paquete UDP/IP, permitiendo que ese frame de Capa 2 se transporte a través del underlay enrutado entre Fabric Edge Nodes, creando efectivamente un segmento Capa 2 de overlay (por VNI) sobre transporte de Capa 3.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What happens from a control-plane perspective when a wired endpoint roams from one Fabric Edge Node to another within the same SD-Access fabric?

options.A: The new Fabric Edge Node updates the Fabric Control Plane node with the endpoint's new location (RLOC), so that subsequent traffic destined for that endpoint is directed to the new Fabric Edge Node instead of the old one, without requiring the endpoint to change its own IP address
options.B: The endpoint is forced to obtain a completely new IP address every time it roams to a different Fabric Edge Node
options.C: Roaming is not supported at all for wired endpoints in SD-Access; only wireless clients can move between access points
options.D: The old Fabric Edge Node continues to receive all traffic for the endpoint indefinitely, with no update ever propagated to the Control Plane node

questions.explanation_es: El nuevo Fabric Edge Node actualiza al Fabric Control Plane node con la nueva ubicación (RLOC) del endpoint, de forma que el tráfico subsiguiente dirigido a ese endpoint se enrute hacia el nuevo Fabric Edge Node en lugar del anterior, sin que el endpoint necesite cambiar su propia dirección IP — esto es posible gracias a la separación identidad/ubicación que provee LISP.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: Why does SD-Access use a routed access design (Layer 3 all the way to the Fabric Edge Node) in its underlay, rather than a traditional Layer 2 access-to-distribution design?

options.A: A routed underlay avoids large Layer 2 broadcast domains and STP-related convergence concerns in the underlay, providing fast, predictable IP-based convergence, while all the segmentation/policy flexibility traditionally requiring Layer 2 extension is instead handled by the VXLAN overlay and SGTs
options.B: A routed access design was chosen purely because it requires less IP addressing than a Layer 2 design
options.C: A routed underlay was chosen because Layer 3 protocols cannot experience any form of network loop, making STP entirely irrelevant to the design's benefits
options.D: Routed access is used only because it is a mandatory requirement for connecting wireless access points, with no benefit for wired forwarding

questions.explanation_es: Un underlay enrutado evita dominios de broadcast de Capa 2 grandes y preocupaciones de convergencia relacionadas con STP en el underlay, dando una convergencia rápida y predecible basada en IP, mientras que toda la flexibilidad de segmentación/política que tradicionalmente requería extender Capa 2 la maneja en cambio el overlay VXLAN junto con los SGT.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What is the significance of an 'anycast gateway' in SD-Access, configured identically on every Fabric Edge Node for a given subnet/VN?

options.A: An anycast gateway means every Fabric Edge Node in the fabric uses the exact same default gateway IP and virtual MAC for a given subnet, allowing an endpoint to roam to any Fabric Edge Node within that subnet's virtual network and keep using the exact same default gateway address, without needing any FHRP protocol like HSRP or VRRP
options.B: An anycast gateway refers to a single, physically centralized router that all fabric traffic must always pass through no matter where the endpoint is located
options.C: Anycast gateway is a wireless-only concept and has no meaning for wired Fabric Edge Nodes
options.D: An anycast gateway requires manually configuring a different gateway IP per Fabric Edge Node, defeating the purpose of a consistent addressing scheme

questions.explanation_es: El anycast gateway significa que todos los Fabric Edge Node de la fabric usan la misma IP y MAC virtual de gateway para una subred dada, permitiendo que un endpoint pueda estar conectado (o moverse) a cualquier Fabric Edge Node de esa virtual network y seguir usando exactamente la misma dirección de gateway, sin necesitar un protocolo FHRP tradicional como HSRP o VRRP.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: When SD-Access enforces SGACL (Security Group ACL) policy, at which point in the data path is that policy typically enforced?

options.A: SGACL policy is enforced only at the Fabric Border Node, regardless of where the source and destination endpoints are actually located within the fabric
options.B: SGACL enforcement typically occurs at the egress Fabric Edge Node (closest to the destination endpoint), which evaluates the source SGT carried in the VXLAN header against the destination SGT/policy matrix before forwarding the traffic to the destination
options.C: SGACL policy is only ever enforced centrally on the Fabric Control Plane node, which physically intercepts every packet before it reaches any Fabric Edge Node
options.D: SGACL enforcement requires a separate physical firewall appliance inserted between every pair of communicating endpoints

questions.explanation_es: La aplicación de SGACL típicamente ocurre en el Fabric Edge Node de egreso (el más cercano al endpoint destino), que evalúa el SGT de origen transportado en el encabezado VXLAN contra la matriz de política/SGT destino antes de reenviar el tráfico al destino final.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: How does SD-Access typically integrate wireless traffic into the fabric's data plane when using a fabric-enabled Wireless LAN Controller (WLC)?

options.A: Wireless traffic in a fabric-enabled deployment is VXLAN-encapsulated at the fabric-enabled Access Point (or at the Fabric Edge Node it connects through) and carried over the same fabric overlay used for wired traffic, rather than being tunneled back to the WLC using traditional CAPWAP data tunneling
options.B: Wireless traffic can never be integrated into an SD-Access fabric under any circumstances; SD-Access is a wired-only architecture
options.C: Wireless traffic is always sent unencapsulated in plaintext directly onto the underlay with no VXLAN involvement whatsoever
options.D: Wireless clients must obtain a completely separate, non-fabric IP addressing scheme that is entirely disconnected from the wired fabric's virtual networks

questions.explanation_es: En un despliegue con fabric habilitada, el tráfico inalámbrico se encapsula en VXLAN en el access point (o en el Fabric Edge Node al que se conecta) y se transporta sobre el mismo overlay de la fabric usado para tráfico cableado, en lugar de tunelizarse de vuelta al WLC vía CAPWAP tradicional — así unifica el tratamiento de política entre cableado e inalámbrico.

questions.name: SD-Access control/data plane
questions.question: What advantage does separating the control plane (LISP-based mapping) from the data plane (VXLAN forwarding) provide in SD-Access, similar to the general SDN philosophy?

options.A: This separation provides no practical advantage and exists purely for historical/legacy reasons carried over from older Cisco products
options.B: Separating control and data planes allows endpoint location/identity information to be managed and updated centrally and efficiently (via the Control Plane node), while actual packet forwarding remains distributed and fast at each Fabric Edge Node, avoiding the need for every switch to flood-and-learn or maintain a full picture of every endpoint in the fabric
options.C: This separation means the data plane no longer needs any IP addressing at all
options.D: This separation exists only to allow SD-Access to be marketed as 'software-defined' with no actual technical benefit

questions.explanation_es: Separar el plano de control (mapeo basado en LISP) del plano de datos (reenvío VXLAN) permite gestionar y actualizar la información de identidad/ubicación de endpoints de forma centralizada y eficiente (vía el Control Plane node), mientras el reenvío real de paquetes permanece distribuido y rápido en cada Fabric Edge Node, evitando que cada switch tenga que hacer flood-and-learn o mantener una imagen completa de cada endpoint de la fabric.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When an SD-Access fabric needs to advertise its internal virtual network subnets to a traditional routed core outside the fabric, what typically happens at the Fabric Border Node?

options.A: The Border Node redistributes or advertises the fabric's VXLAN-encapsulated routes into standard IP routing (e.g., via BGP or OSPF) toward the external network, translating the fabric's internal reachability information into a form the traditional routed network understands
options.B: The Border Node simply drops all traffic destined for any address outside the fabric, since fabrics are designed to be fully isolated from external networks by default
options.C: The Border Node requires every external router to run LISP natively before any interoperability is possible
options.D: The Border Node converts all external traffic into VXLAN before it even reaches the fabric boundary, regardless of whether the external device supports VXLAN

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node redistribuye o anuncia las rutas internas de la fabric (VXLAN) hacia el enrutamiento IP estándar (por ejemplo, vía BGP u OSPF) hacia la red externa, traduciendo la información de alcanzabilidad interna de la fabric a una forma que la red enrutada tradicional entienda — es el punto de traducción entre ambos mundos.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why is a Fusion Router (or Fusion Firewall) often needed when SD-Access virtual networks (VRFs) need to communicate with resources in a shared services VRF or the traditional network's global routing table?

options.A: VRFs are isolated from each other and from the global routing table by design; a Fusion device performs controlled route leaking (importing/exporting routes) between the VRFs and the external network, since simply attaching them to the same Border Node does not automatically merge their routing tables
options.B: A Fusion Router is needed only to provide DHCP services, with no relationship to route leaking or VRF communication at all
options.C: Fusion Routers exist purely to physically convert copper cabling into fiber cabling at the fabric boundary
options.D: A Fusion Router is required only when the fabric has exactly one virtual network configured, and becomes unnecessary once a second VN is added

questions.explanation_es: Las VRFs están aisladas entre sí y de la tabla de enrutamiento global por diseño; un dispositivo Fusion realiza route leaking controlado (importando/exportando rutas) entre las VRFs y la red externa, ya que simplemente conectarlas al mismo Border Node no fusiona automáticamente sus tablas de enrutamiento.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: How can SGT information be preserved when traffic needs to leave the SD-Access fabric and cross a segment of traditional (non-fabric) network before reaching another fabric-aware or ISE-integrated device?

options.A: SGT information is always permanently lost the moment traffic leaves any fabric, with absolutely no way to preserve or propagate it across non-fabric segments under any circumstances
options.B: SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) can be used to propagate IP-address-to-SGT bindings to devices that lack inline SGT tagging support, allowing policy enforcement to be extended (in a limited, IP-binding-based way) even across parts of the network that don't natively carry SGTs in the data plane
options.C: SGT information can only be preserved if the entire traditional network segment is physically replaced with fabric-capable switches first
options.D: SGT information is automatically converted into a VLAN ID whenever it crosses into a non-fabric segment, with no configuration required

questions.explanation_es: SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) permite propagar los bindings de IP-a-SGT hacia dispositivos que no soportan tagging inline de SGT, permitiendo extender la aplicación de política (de forma limitada, basada en bindings de IP) incluso a través de partes de la red que no transportan SGTs nativamente en el plano de datos.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: In a phased SD-Access migration, why might an organization choose to migrate by 'IP pool' rather than migrating an entire physical site all at once?

options.A: IP pool-based migration is purely a licensing requirement with no operational reasoning behind it
options.B: Migrating by IP pool allows specific groups of endpoints (e.g., a particular department or VLAN's address range) to be moved into the fabric incrementally, limiting the blast radius and complexity of each migration step, while other pools continue operating on the traditional network until they too are migrated
options.C: IP pool-based migration requires renumbering the entire campus to a single subnet before any migration can begin
options.D: IP pools are only relevant to wireless clients and have no bearing on how wired migration is phased

questions.explanation_es: Migrar por IP pool permite mover grupos específicos de endpoints (por ejemplo, el rango de direcciones de un departamento o VLAN en particular) a la fabric de forma incremental, limitando el radio de impacto y la complejidad de cada paso de migración, mientras el resto sigue operando en la red tradicional hasta que también se migre.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What consideration is important when connecting a traditional Layer 2 access switch (non-fabric) to a Fabric Edge Node as part of an interoperability/migration design?

options.A: No special consideration is needed at all; a traditional switch can be plugged directly into a Fabric Edge Node with zero configuration and instantly gains full fabric capabilities, including VXLAN encapsulation, automatically
options.B: The traditional switch's VLANs and trunking need to be properly mapped/extended to correspond with the correct IP pools and virtual networks configured on the fabric side, since the traditional switch itself has no awareness of VXLAN, SGTs, or the fabric's LISP control plane
options.C: Traditional switches can never be connected to a Fabric Edge Node under any circumstances; only fabric-capable hardware may connect there
options.D: Connecting a traditional switch to a Fabric Edge Node automatically disables SGACL enforcement fabric-wide

questions.explanation_es: Las VLANs y el trunking del switch tradicional deben mapearse/extenderse correctamente para corresponder con los IP pools y virtual networks configurados del lado de la fabric, ya que el switch tradicional en sí no tiene conocimiento de VXLAN, SGTs, ni del plano de control LISP de la fabric — la traducción ocurre en el Fabric Edge Node al que se conecta.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why is it generally recommended to plan IP addressing/subnetting carefully before beginning an SD-Access migration from a traditional network?

options.A: IP addressing has no bearing whatsoever on SD-Access migration planning, since the fabric automatically renumbers every device transparently with zero pre-planning required
options.B: SD-Access typically maps subnets to IP pools associated with specific virtual networks, so a clean, well-planned addressing scheme makes it easier to logically group endpoints into the correct virtual networks and simplifies the eventual mapping between legacy VLANs/subnets and fabric IP pools
options.C: IP addressing only matters for wireless clients in an SD-Access deployment and has no relevance to wired endpoint migration
options.D: Careful IP planning is only necessary if the organization plans to use IPv6 exclusively, with no relevance to IPv4-only deployments

questions.explanation_es: SD-Access típicamente mapea subredes a IP pools asociados a virtual networks específicas, así que un esquema de direccionamiento limpio y bien planeado facilita agrupar lógicamente a los endpoints en la virtual network correcta y simplifica el mapeo eventual entre VLANs/subredes legacy y los IP pools de la fabric.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What role can a traditional distribution-layer switch play temporarily during a phased migration, before it is eventually replaced or converted into a Fabric Border/Edge role?

options.A: It can continue serving non-migrated access switches and VLANs exactly as before, connecting into the fabric via the Border Node so that migrated and non-migrated portions of the campus remain interconnected throughout the transition period
options.B: A traditional distribution switch must be physically powered off the instant any part of the campus begins migrating to SD-Access, with no coexistence period possible
options.C: Traditional distribution switches automatically gain full SD-Access fabric awareness the moment SD-Access is enabled anywhere in the campus, with no configuration required
options.D: A traditional distribution switch can only interoperate with a fabric if it is running the exact same software version as every Fabric Edge Node

questions.explanation_es: Un switch de distribución tradicional puede seguir sirviendo a los switches de acceso y VLANs aún no migrados exactamente como antes, conectándose a la fabric a través del Border Node, de forma que las porciones migradas y no migradas del campus permanezcan interconectadas durante todo el período de transición.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: When extending shared services (such as DNS, DHCP, or an ISE server) that live in the traditional network's global routing table to be reachable from within SD-Access virtual networks, what is a common design approach?

options.A: Shared services must be physically duplicated and re-hosted separately inside every single virtual network, since cross-VN or cross-VRF reachability is technically impossible under any configuration
options.B: Route leaking is configured (often via a Fusion device or route-target import/export) so that each virtual network's VRF can reach the shared services subnet in the global table, without fully merging every VN's routing table together
options.C: Shared services are always automatically reachable from every virtual network with no configuration required, since VRF isolation does not apply to well-known service ports like DNS or DHCP
options.D: Shared services can only be reached by manually connecting a physical Ethernet cable from every access switch directly to the DHCP server

questions.explanation_es: Se configura route leaking (a menudo vía un dispositivo Fusion o import/export de route-targets) para que la VRF de cada virtual network pueda alcanzar la subred de servicios compartidos en la tabla global, sin fusionar completamente la tabla de enrutamiento de cada VN — un patrón de diseño común para servicios como DNS, DHCP o ISE.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: What is a key reason SD-Access migrations are typically done incrementally rather than as a single 'flash cut' across an entire large campus?

options.A: Incremental migration is purely a marketing recommendation with no real operational benefit over a single flash cut
options.B: An incremental approach limits risk by validating fabric behavior, policy, and interoperability on a smaller scale first, allows lessons learned to inform later phases, and reduces the potential impact/blast radius if an issue is discovered, compared to converting an entire large campus in one maintenance window
options.C: Flash-cut migrations are technically impossible for any Cisco product due to a hard-coded software limitation
options.D: Incremental migration is required because SD-Access fabrics are limited to a maximum of exactly one switch per fabric

questions.explanation_es: Un enfoque incremental limita el riesgo al validar el comportamiento de la fabric, la política y la interoperabilidad a menor escala primero, permite que las lecciones aprendidas informen fases posteriores, y reduce el impacto potencial si se descubre un problema, comparado con convertir todo un campus grande en una sola ventana de mantenimiento.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: How does a Fabric Border Node typically handle a default route or 'internet-bound' traffic originating from inside the SD-Access fabric?

options.A: The Border Node commonly advertises a default route (or specific external routes) into the fabric's control plane, so that internal fabric traffic destined for unknown/external destinations (like the internet) is directed toward the Border Node for handoff to the traditional network/internet edge
options.B: Internet-bound traffic from inside the fabric is always silently dropped, since fabrics have no concept of a default route by design
options.C: Every individual Fabric Edge Node must have its own direct physical connection to the internet, with no role for the Border Node in internet connectivity at all
options.D: The Border Node requires every endpoint to manually configure its own static default route pointing directly at an ISP router

questions.explanation_es: El Border Node comúnmente anuncia una ruta default (o rutas externas específicas) hacia el plano de control de la fabric, de forma que el tráfico interno de la fabric destinado a destinos desconocidos/externos (como internet) se dirija hacia el Border Node para su entrega hacia la red tradicional/borde de internet.

questions.name: Interoperabilidad campus tradicional/SD-Access
questions.question: Why might an organization deploy more than one Fabric Border Node in an SD-Access design that interoperates with a traditional network?

options.A: Multiple Border Nodes are required purely to increase the total VLAN ID range available anywhere in the fabric
options.B: Deploying redundant Border Nodes avoids a single point of failure for external/interoperability connectivity, so the fabric can continue reaching external networks and shared services even if one Border Node fails or needs maintenance
options.C: A fabric can technically have only one Border Node ever, so 'multiple Border Nodes' is not a real deployment option in SD-Access
options.D: Multiple Border Nodes exist solely to allow different wireless SSIDs to be broadcast from different physical locations

questions.explanation_es: Desplegar Border Nodes redundantes evita un punto único de falla para la conectividad externa/de interoperabilidad, de forma que la fabric pueda seguir alcanzando redes externas y servicios compartidos aunque un Border Node falle o requiera mantenimiento — un patrón de alta disponibilidad habitual en diseños de producción.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the DiffServ (Differentiated Services) QoS model, as opposed to IntServ (Integrated Services)?

options.A: DiffServ classifies and marks traffic into a small number of forwarding classes (using DSCP) and applies per-hop behaviors at each device, providing scalable QoS without requiring per-flow signaling or reservation across the entire path, unlike IntServ's RSVP-based per-flow reservation model
options.B: DiffServ requires every router along the path to reserve dedicated bandwidth for every individual flow before any traffic can be sent, exactly like IntServ
options.C: DiffServ only applies to wireless networks and has no relevance to wired QoS design
options.D: DiffServ and IntServ are simply two different names for the exact same mechanism with no technical distinction

questions.explanation_es: DiffServ clasifica y marca el tráfico en un número pequeño de clases de reenvío (usando DSCP) y aplica comportamientos por salto (per-hop behavior) en cada dispositivo, dando QoS escalable sin necesitar señalización o reserva por flujo a lo largo de todo el camino — a diferencia de IntServ, que usa RSVP para reservar recursos por flujo individual, lo cual escala mucho peor en redes grandes.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does the term 'trust boundary' mean in a QoS design, and where is it typically placed?

options.A: The trust boundary is the point in the network where markings (CoS/DSCP) applied by an upstream device or endpoint are either accepted as-is or re-classified/re-marked; it is typically placed as close to the network edge as possible (e.g., at the access-layer switch port) to avoid trusting markings from untrusted end-user devices
options.B: The trust boundary refers exclusively to the physical distance (in meters) that fiber cabling can carry a QoS-marked signal without amplification
options.C: The trust boundary is a firewall rule that has no relationship to DSCP or CoS marking at all
options.D: The trust boundary must always be placed at the network core, and can never be placed at the access layer

questions.explanation_es: El trust boundary es el punto de la red donde se decide si aceptar tal cual las marcas (CoS/DSCP) aplicadas por un dispositivo o endpoint anterior, o volver a clasificar/remarcar el tráfico; típicamente se ubica lo más cerca posible del borde de la red (por ejemplo, en el puerto del switch de acceso) para evitar confiar en las marcas puestas por dispositivos de usuario final no confiables.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Which queuing mechanism is specifically designed to give strict priority to a designated class of traffic (such as voice), ensuring it is always serviced first, ahead of other queues, up to a configured bandwidth limit?

options.A: FIFO (First In, First Out) queuing, which treats every packet from every class identically with no prioritization
options.B: LLQ (Low Latency Queuing), which adds a strict-priority queue on top of CBWFQ, so traffic assigned to that priority queue (like voice) is always serviced ahead of the other CBWFQ classes, within a configured policed bandwidth limit to prevent it from starving other traffic
options.C: WRED (Weighted Random Early Detection), which is a congestion avoidance mechanism, not a queuing/scheduling mechanism
options.D: Round-robin queuing, which services every queue in strict rotating order regardless of any traffic's latency sensitivity

questions.explanation_es: LLQ (Low Latency Queuing) agrega una cola de prioridad estricta sobre CBWFQ, de forma que el tráfico asignado a esa cola de prioridad (como voz) siempre se atienda antes que las demás clases de CBWFQ, dentro de un límite de ancho de banda policiado configurado para evitar que ahogue al resto del tráfico.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does CBWFQ (Class-Based Weighted Fair Queuing) provide that basic WFQ (Weighted Fair Queuing) does not?

options.A: CBWFQ allows the administrator to explicitly define traffic classes (via class-maps matching specific criteria) and assign a guaranteed minimum bandwidth or percentage to each class, whereas basic WFQ automatically classifies flows based on characteristics like IP address/port with no administrator-defined classes or guaranteed bandwidth allocation
options.B: CBWFQ and WFQ are identical mechanisms, differing only in which IOS command is used to configure them
options.C: CBWFQ can only be applied to wireless interfaces, while WFQ can only be applied to wired interfaces
options.D: CBWFQ removes the ability to guarantee any bandwidth at all, while WFQ guarantees 100% of bandwidth to every flow simultaneously

questions.explanation_es: CBWFQ permite que el administrador defina explícitamente clases de tráfico (mediante class-maps que hacen match con criterios específicos) y asigne un ancho de banda mínimo garantizado o un porcentaje a cada clase, mientras que el WFQ básico clasifica flujos automáticamente según características como IP/puerto, sin clases definidas por el administrador ni garantía de ancho de banda por clase.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between traffic 'shaping' and traffic 'policing' when traffic exceeds a configured rate?

options.A: Shaping and policing are exactly the same mechanism, differing only in which IOS command syntax is used to enable them
options.B: Policing typically drops (or re-marks) traffic that exceeds the configured rate immediately, with no buffering, resulting in a 'hard' rate limit; shaping buffers and delays excess traffic to smooth bursts out over time so the traffic conforms to the rate without necessarily dropping it, at the cost of added latency/jitter for the delayed packets
options.C: Shaping can only be applied on inbound traffic, and policing can only be applied on outbound traffic, with no exceptions
options.D: Policing always adds latency by buffering excess traffic, while shaping always drops excess traffic immediately with no buffering

questions.explanation_es: El policing típicamente descarta (o remarca) el tráfico que excede la tasa configurada de inmediato, sin buffer, resultando en un límite de tasa 'duro'; el shaping en cambio almacena y retrasa el tráfico excedente para suavizar las ráfagas a lo largo del tiempo, haciendo que el tráfico se ajuste a la tasa sin necesariamente descartarlo, a costa de agregar latencia/jitter a los paquetes retrasados.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What problem does WRED (Weighted Random Early Detection) address, and how does it work at a high level?

options.A: WRED prevents TCP global synchronization and worsening congestion by proactively and randomly dropping some packets before a queue becomes completely full, with the drop probability increasing (and weighted by factors like DSCP/IP precedence) as the queue fills, rather than waiting until the queue overflows and dropping many packets from many flows all at once (tail drop)
options.B: WRED guarantees that no packet will ever be dropped under any level of network congestion, no matter how severe
options.C: WRED only operates on wireless interfaces and has no application to wired congestion avoidance
options.D: WRED works by physically reducing the interface's link speed whenever congestion is detected

questions.explanation_es: WRED previene la sincronización global de TCP y el empeoramiento de la congestión, descartando de forma proactiva y aleatoria algunos paquetes antes de que la cola se llene completamente, con probabilidad de descarte creciente (ponderada por factores como DSCP/IP precedence) a medida que la cola se llena, en lugar de esperar a que la cola desborde y descartar muchos paquetes de muchos flujos de golpe (tail drop).

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: According to Cisco's QoS best-practice marking recommendations, which DSCP class is typically used to mark call-signaling traffic (e.g., SCCP/SIP), as distinct from the voice bearer (RTP) traffic itself?

options.A: CS3 (Class Selector 3) is the commonly recommended marking for call-signaling traffic, which is treated with a lower priority guarantee than the EF-marked voice bearer traffic but still receives preferential treatment over best-effort data
options.B: Call-signaling traffic uses the exact same EF marking as voice bearer traffic, with no distinction made between the two at all
options.C: Call-signaling traffic is always marked with the lowest possible DSCP value (0, best-effort), identical to ordinary web browsing traffic
options.D: Call-signaling traffic cannot be marked with DSCP at all and must rely exclusively on Layer 2 CoS marking

questions.explanation_es: CS3 (Class Selector 3) es la marca comúnmente recomendada para tráfico de señalización de llamadas, que recibe un trato con menor prioridad garantizada que el tráfico portador de voz marcado con EF, pero aún así recibe trato preferencial frente al tráfico de datos best-effort.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the relationship between Layer 2 CoS (Class of Service, in an 802.1Q tag's PCP field) and Layer 3 DSCP marking?

options.A: CoS and DSCP are completely unrelated fields that can never be mapped to one another under any circumstances
options.B: CoS is a 3-bit field carried at Layer 2 (in the 802.1Q PCP field), while DSCP is a 6-bit field carried at Layer 3 (in the IP header's ToS/DS byte); network devices often map between the two (CoS-to-DSCP and DSCP-to-CoS) as traffic crosses the Layer 2/Layer 3 boundary, since CoS marking does not survive being routed while DSCP does
options.C: DSCP only exists in IPv6 and has no equivalent field in IPv4, making CoS-to-DSCP mapping technically impossible for IPv4 traffic
options.D: CoS is an 8-bit field, and DSCP is a 2-bit field, making a one-to-one mapping between them numerically impossible

questions.explanation_es: CoS es un campo de 3 bits transportado en Capa 2 (en el campo PCP del tag 802.1Q), mientras que DSCP es un campo de 6 bits transportado en Capa 3 (en el byte ToS/DS del encabezado IP); los dispositivos suelen mapear entre ambos (CoS-a-DSCP y DSCP-a-CoS) al cruzar el límite Capa 2/Capa 3, ya que la marca CoS no sobrevive al ser enrutada, mientras que DSCP sí.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why is jitter (variation in packet delay) particularly problematic for real-time applications like voice and video, even more so than a moderate constant delay?

options.A: Jitter has no actual effect on voice or video quality whatsoever and is purely a theoretical concern with no practical impact
options.B: Real-time applications play out received packets at a steady rate for the listener/viewer; jitter buffers can compensate for a limited amount of variation, but excessive jitter can cause packets to arrive too late to be used, leading to audio/video glitches, gaps, or dropped frames, even if the average delay itself is acceptable
options.C: Jitter only affects text-based protocols like HTTP and has no bearing on audio or video streams at all
options.D: Jitter is measured exclusively in bytes, not in time, making it unrelated to any timing-sensitive application

questions.explanation_es: Las aplicaciones en tiempo real reproducen los paquetes recibidos a un ritmo constante para el oyente/espectador; los buffers de jitter pueden compensar una variación limitada, pero un jitter excesivo puede hacer que los paquetes lleguen demasiado tarde para usarse, causando cortes o glitches de audio/video, incluso si el retardo promedio en sí es aceptable.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the Cisco-recommended best-practice DSCP marking for interactive video (e.g., video conferencing) traffic, as distinct from voice?

options.A: AF41 (Assured Forwarding class 4, low drop precedence) is the commonly recommended marking for interactive video, giving it strong (though not strict-priority-queue-guaranteed like EF) preferential treatment distinct from voice bearer traffic
options.B: Interactive video always uses the exact same EF marking as voice, with Cisco best practice making no distinction between the two traffic types whatsoever
options.C: Interactive video is always marked as best-effort (DSCP 0), identical to ordinary web browsing, since video is considered non-critical by Cisco best practice
options.D: Interactive video cannot be marked with any DSCP value under any Cisco best-practice recommendation and must rely solely on physical bandwidth reservation

questions.explanation_es: AF41 (Assured Forwarding clase 4, baja precedencia de descarte) es la marca comúnmente recomendada para video interactivo, dándole un trato preferencial fuerte (aunque no con la garantía de cola de prioridad estricta que sí tiene EF), distinto del tráfico portador de voz.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: In QoS policy configuration on Cisco IOS, what is the relationship between a class-map, a policy-map, and a service-policy?

options.A: A class-map defines the traffic classification criteria (what to match); a policy-map defines the QoS actions (e.g., bandwidth, priority, marking) to apply to one or more classes referenced from class-maps; and a service-policy applies a given policy-map to a specific interface (inbound or outbound)
options.B: Class-map, policy-map, and service-policy are three interchangeable names for the exact same single configuration object, with no functional difference between them
options.C: A service-policy defines traffic classification, while class-map and policy-map are only used for interface speed/duplex negotiation, unrelated to QoS
options.D: A policy-map can only be applied globally to the entire router and can never be applied to an individual interface

questions.explanation_es: El class-map define los criterios de clasificación del tráfico (qué hacer match); el policy-map define las acciones de QoS (ancho de banda, prioridad, marcado) a aplicar a una o más clases referenciadas desde los class-maps; y el service-policy aplica un policy-map determinado a una interfaz específica (entrante o saliente) — la jerarquía típica de configuración de QoS en Cisco IOS.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why does Cisco best practice generally recommend classifying and marking traffic as close to the source as possible (e.g., at the endpoint or access-layer switch), rather than only at a central point like the WAN edge?

options.A: Marking close to the source has no actual benefit and is purely a stylistic convention with no operational reasoning behind it
options.B: Marking traffic early allows every downstream device along the path to make consistent QoS decisions (queuing, dropping, shaping) based on that marking from the very first hop, rather than treating all traffic as best-effort until it reaches a distant central point, which could allow congestion to occur before any prioritization is ever applied
options.C: Marking traffic close to the source is only relevant for wireless traffic and has no bearing on wired network design at all
options.D: Cisco best practice actually recommends the opposite: never marking traffic until it reaches the WAN edge, to avoid any risk of early misclassification

questions.explanation_es: Marcar el tráfico temprano permite que todos los dispositivos aguas abajo en el camino tomen decisiones de QoS consistentes (colas, descartes, shaping) basadas en esa marca desde el primer salto, en lugar de tratar todo el tráfico como best-effort hasta que llegue a un punto central lejano, lo cual podría permitir que ocurra congestión antes de que se aplique cualquier priorización.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does 'admission control' typically refer to in the context of voice/video QoS design (e.g., via CAC — Call Admission Control)?

options.A: Admission control refers to a physical security badge reader that grants employees access to the building where network equipment is stored
options.B: Admission control (CAC) limits the number of simultaneous voice/video calls/sessions allowed over a given constrained-bandwidth link, rejecting or redirecting new call attempts once the configured bandwidth threshold for that traffic class would be exceeded, protecting the quality of calls already in progress
options.C: Admission control refers exclusively to which VLANs are permitted to trunk across a given switch port, unrelated to voice or video traffic
options.D: Admission control guarantees unlimited simultaneous calls of any quality on any link, regardless of available bandwidth

questions.explanation_es: El control de admisión de llamadas (CAC) limita el número de llamadas/sesiones de voz o video simultáneas permitidas sobre un enlace de ancho de banda limitado, rechazando o redirigiendo nuevos intentos de llamada una vez que se superaría el umbral de ancho de banda configurado para esa clase de tráfico, protegiendo la calidad de las llamadas ya en curso.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is a key QoS design consideration specific to wireless LANs (e.g., using WMM — Wi-Fi Multimedia) compared to wired QoS?

options.A: Wireless QoS is identical in every respect to wired QoS, since the shared wireless medium behaves exactly like a dedicated switched Ethernet link with no contention involved
options.B: Because wireless is a shared, contention-based medium (unlike a dedicated switched Ethernet link), wireless QoS mechanisms like WMM adjust channel access parameters (such as contention window sizes) to give higher-priority traffic classes a statistically better chance of gaining access to the shared airtime, in addition to queuing/marking concepts similar to wired QoS
options.C: Wireless networks are technically incapable of supporting any form of QoS marking or prioritization under any circumstances
options.D: WMM only applies to wired Ethernet ports and has no relevance to actual over-the-air wireless transmissions

questions.explanation_es: Como el medio inalámbrico es compartido y basado en contención (a diferencia de un enlace Ethernet conmutado dedicado), mecanismos de QoS inalámbrico como WMM ajustan parámetros de acceso al canal (como el tamaño de la ventana de contención) para darle a las clases de tráfico de mayor prioridad una probabilidad estadísticamente mejor de acceder al medio compartido, además de conceptos de colas/marcado similares a los del QoS cableado.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why is it generally considered a QoS design mistake to mark a large portion of an organization's traffic (e.g., most applications) as high priority or EF?

options.A: There is no downside to marking most traffic as high priority; doing so always improves the performance of every application simultaneously with no trade-off
options.B: If most traffic is marked as high priority, the priority marking loses its meaning as a differentiator — during actual congestion, a priority queue that is itself oversubscribed with too much 'high priority' traffic can no longer reliably protect the truly latency-sensitive applications (like voice) it was meant to protect
options.C: Marking traffic as high priority is purely cosmetic and has zero effect on actual queuing or dropping behavior on any Cisco platform
options.D: QoS marking is limited to exactly one single traffic class per router globally, so marking multiple applications as high priority is not technically possible in the first place

questions.explanation_es: Si la mayor parte del tráfico se marca como alta prioridad, la marca pierde su valor como diferenciador — durante congestión real, una cola de prioridad sobre-suscrita con demasiado tráfico 'de alta prioridad' ya no puede proteger de forma confiable a las aplicaciones realmente sensibles a la latencia (como voz) que se suponía debía proteger. Por eso EF debe reservarse estrictamente para voz.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What does the term 'tail drop' refer to in the context of interface queuing, and why is it generally considered less desirable than WRED for TCP-heavy traffic?

options.A: Tail drop happens when a queue is completely full and any newly arriving packet is simply discarded because there is no room left; for TCP flows, this can cause many flows to experience loss and reduce their send rate at roughly the same time (TCP global synchronization), leading to oscillating underutilization and re-congestion of the link
options.B: Tail drop refers to physically disconnecting the last few centimeters of an Ethernet cable to intentionally reduce signal quality
options.C: Tail drop only occurs on wireless interfaces and has no equivalent behavior on any wired interface queue
options.D: Tail drop guarantees that TCP flows will never reduce their sending rate, regardless of how full the queue becomes

questions.explanation_es: Tail drop ocurre cuando una cola está completamente llena y cualquier paquete nuevo que llega simplemente se descarta porque no queda espacio; para flujos TCP, esto puede hacer que muchos flujos experimenten pérdida y reduzcan su tasa de envío casi al mismo tiempo (sincronización global de TCP), provocando una oscilación de subutilización y recongestión del enlace — por eso WRED suele preferirse para tráfico dominado por TCP.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: In an end-to-end QoS design spanning a campus LAN and a WAN edge, why is it important that DSCP markings be preserved (not stripped or reset) as traffic crosses from the LAN into the WAN?

options.A: DSCP markings are automatically regenerated identically at every hop regardless of any configuration, making preservation an automatic, unavoidable behavior with nothing to design for
options.B: If markings are stripped or reset at the LAN/WAN boundary, the WAN edge device and every downstream device across the WAN would be unable to apply the correct differentiated treatment to that traffic, effectively defeating the purpose of having classified and marked it consistently within the campus in the first place
options.C: DSCP markings only matter within a single VLAN and have no relevance once traffic leaves that VLAN, regardless of whether it crosses into a WAN
options.D: Preserving DSCP markings across the LAN/WAN boundary is prohibited by RFC 2474 and must always be explicitly reset

questions.explanation_es: Si las marcas se eliminan o reinician en el límite LAN/WAN, el equipo de borde WAN y todos los dispositivos aguas abajo a través de la WAN no podrían aplicar el trato diferenciado correcto a ese tráfico, anulando efectivamente el propósito de haberlo clasificado y marcado de forma consistente dentro del campus — por eso preservar DSCP de extremo a extremo es un principio de diseño clave.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is a 'conform-action' and 'exceed-action' in the context of a Cisco policing configuration (e.g., using CIR — Committed Information Rate)?

options.A: Conform-action and exceed-action refer exclusively to which VLAN a packet belongs to, with no relationship to rate or bandwidth at all
options.B: The conform-action specifies what to do with traffic that stays within the configured committed rate (e.g., transmit as-is), while the exceed-action specifies what to do with traffic that goes above that rate (e.g., drop it, or re-mark it to a lower-priority DSCP/CoS value before transmitting)
options.C: Conform-action and exceed-action are two names for the exact same action, applied redundantly for legacy compatibility reasons
options.D: Conform-action only applies to inbound traffic, and exceed-action only applies to traffic that has already been dropped, making it moot

questions.explanation_es: El conform-action especifica qué hacer con el tráfico que se mantiene dentro de la tasa comprometida configurada (por ejemplo, transmitirlo tal cual), mientras que el exceed-action especifica qué hacer con el tráfico que supera esa tasa (por ejemplo, descartarlo, o remarcarlo a un valor DSCP/CoS de menor prioridad antes de transmitirlo) — la base de una configuración de policing con CIR en Cisco IOS.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: Why might a service provider apply policing (rather than shaping) at the ingress of their network for a customer's traffic entering via an MPLS or internet circuit?

options.A: A service provider always prefers shaping over policing at every ingress point in every scenario, with policing never actually being used at the network edge
options.B: Policing at ingress lets the provider enforce a hard contracted rate limit (e.g., a customer's purchased bandwidth) immediately, without the provider's own network having to buffer/delay a customer's excess traffic — protecting the provider's shared infrastructure from a single customer exceeding their agreed rate, at the cost of dropping (rather than smoothing) that excess traffic
options.C: Policing is only technically possible on customer-owned equipment and can never be applied on provider-owned equipment
options.D: Policing at ingress guarantees that a customer's traffic will never experience any packet loss under any circumstances

questions.explanation_es: El policing en el ingreso le permite al proveedor aplicar de inmediato un límite de tasa contratado (por ejemplo, el ancho de banda comprado por el cliente), sin que la propia red del proveedor tenga que hacer buffer/retrasar el tráfico excedente del cliente — protegiendo la infraestructura compartida del proveedor de que un solo cliente exceda su tasa acordada, a costa de descartar (en vez de suavizar) ese tráfico excedente.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: According to Cisco's QoS baseline marking recommendations, roughly how many traffic classes (application categories) does the model typically define for consistent enterprise-wide marking?

options.A: Exactly one single class, since Cisco best practice recommends treating all traffic identically with no differentiation whatsoever
options.B: Cisco's QoS baseline defines a fairly granular set of traffic classes (covering categories such as voice, broadcast video, real-time interactive, multimedia conferencing, network control, signaling, and various data classes like transactional/bulk/best-effort/scavenger), each intended to receive consistent marking and treatment across the enterprise
options.C: Exactly two classes only: 'important' and 'unimportant', with no further granularity defined by Cisco
options.D: The number of classes is fixed permanently at exactly 256, matching the maximum possible DSCP value

questions.explanation_es: El QoS baseline de Cisco define un conjunto bastante granular de clases de tráfico (voz, video broadcast, tiempo real interactivo, conferencia multimedia, control de red, señalización, y varias clases de datos como transaccional/bulk/best-effort/scavenger), cada una pensada para recibir marcado y trato consistente en toda la empresa — no es simplemente 'importante vs no importante'.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: What is the 'scavenger' traffic class typically used for in a Cisco QoS marking scheme, and how is it usually marked?

options.A: The scavenger class is used for the organization's most business-critical, latency-sensitive applications, and is always marked with EF, identical to voice
options.B: The scavenger class (commonly marked with CS1) is used for traffic that is explicitly considered 'less than best-effort' — such as recreational or non-business applications — so that during periods of congestion, this traffic is the first to be starved/dropped, protecting bandwidth for all other legitimate business traffic classes
options.C: The scavenger class refers exclusively to network management/monitoring traffic like SNMP and syslog, which Cisco recommends marking with the highest possible priority
options.D: Scavenger-class traffic is always given strictly more guaranteed bandwidth than any other class in the QoS baseline

questions.explanation_es: La clase scavenger (comúnmente marcada con CS1) se usa para tráfico explícitamente considerado 'menos que best-effort' — como aplicaciones recreativas o no relacionadas con el negocio — de forma que durante períodos de congestión, ese tráfico sea el primero en verse limitado/descartado, protegiendo el ancho de banda para el resto de las clases de tráfico legítimas del negocio.

questions.name: QoS
questions.question: In a hub-and-spoke WAN topology with a high-bandwidth hub and lower-bandwidth spoke links, why is shaping commonly applied at the hub site toward each spoke, even though the hub's own physical interface may have plenty of bandwidth available?

options.A: Shaping at the hub has no real purpose in a hub-and-spoke design and is never actually recommended by Cisco for this scenario
options.B: Even though the hub interface itself may be fast, each individual spoke's actual access-circuit bandwidth is typically much lower; shaping outbound traffic at the hub toward each spoke's rate prevents overrunning that spoke's slower link and causing uncontrolled tail drops or excessive queuing delay at the spoke's ingress
options.C: Shaping at the hub is only relevant if every spoke has identical bandwidth to the hub itself, with no benefit in a mixed-bandwidth topology
options.D: Shaping at the hub is required only to comply with a licensing restriction, with no actual traffic-management purpose

questions.explanation_es: Aunque la interfaz del hub sea rápida, el ancho de banda real del circuito de acceso de cada spoke suele ser mucho menor; aplicar shaping saliente en el hub ajustado a la tasa de cada spoke evita saturar ese enlace más lento y causar tail drops descontrolados o retardo de cola excesivo en el ingreso del spoke — un patrón de diseño clásico en topologías hub-and-spoke con enlaces de spoke más lentos que el hub.
